issue.description:
proxy/main.go's AdaptiveRateLimiter is a single global token bucket shared by every
caller (documented in docs/plan/plan.md: "A single token-bucket limiter serves all
traffic"). There is no per-agent authentication by design, but that also means one
noisy caller (a runaway NEEDLE worker, a retry storm) can consume the entire
RATE_LIMIT_MAX budget (7 req/s in production - see zai-proxy-v2 env) and starve every
other caller sharing the proxy.

Add lightweight fairness on top of the existing limiter, without adding per-agent auth:
- Key in-flight/waiting requests by a coarse identity signal already available without
  new auth (e.g. source pod IP from cluster-internal DNS, or a caller-supplied
  X-Client-Id header that is not treated as a credential).
- Round-robin or weighted-fair-queue across keys when the global rate is saturated,
  instead of first-come-first-served.
- Expose a per-key wait-time or rejection metric (extend
  zai_proxy_rate_limit_rejections_total with a client label, cardinality-bounded).

Keep the existing global ceiling/EWMA logic (proxy/main.go AdaptiveRateLimiter) as the
outer bound - this is about fairness *within* that budget, not raising it.
issue.title: Add per-source fairness to the global adaptive rate limiter
